newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended Wednesday lower after a slack day in which the market reacted to a strong move upwards on Tuesday and dealers said fears over price pressures in the United States had not been completely allayed.

The Dutch long bond ended around a half a point down, dented by a weak start for U.S. Treasuries, which were hit by the release of strong manufacturing data. Analysts said the figures pointed to continued vigour in consumer demand.
"There is still the feeling that the Fed may do something pre-emptive against the inflationary threat and that's pushing the Dutch market lower," one dealer said.
Debt markets across Europe surged higher on Tuesday after tame U.S. inflation numbers were released but dealers here said the market's move higher had been overdone.
Prices started the morning on the defensive and moved little all day. Wednesday's data did little to spur fresh demand.

Dealers noted pockets of buying at the longer end of the curve, but the spread to Bunds was relatively steady. Along the Guilder curve, the 10-two year spread widened a little to 221. At the shorter end, prices were steadier, the benchmark 6.25 percent July 1998 issue closing just 0.02 points weaker.
